correctness.rationale: In H=M₂(F), write A and B as rank-one outer products. The determinant of their sum factors into the two image and row-space determinants; exactly one vanishes, since vanishing of both would make A and B proportional. The Cayley–Dickson product gives the target (AH+BH) ⊕ (HA+HB)ω and the fixed-h blocks z↦Ahz−Bzh and r↦r(hA−h̄B). In the common-image case, the displayed two rows are independent whenever (a+bt−c,b−d)≠0, which excludes at most one shear parameter; even F₃ has two nonzero candidates. The other block is invertible with determinant 2t(ad−bc). In the common-kernel case, regrouping the four rows and columns of the first block gives two determinants ad−bc and total determinant −(ad−bc)². The second block is right multiplication by the rank-one h(A+B), with both output rows independently in the same one-dimensional row space. Thus the ranks are (2,4) or (4,2) and each slice is onto the stated target. This is an exact image, not just a spanning argument. The word ‘right ideal’ for HA=HB is a handedness slip (it is a left ideal); the actual matrix space and argument are correct. The inspected finite-field program is supplementary and was not executed. Characteristic two and pairs not co-contained in a nondegenerate quaternion composition subalgebra remain outside the proof.
